memory_update.text: INOD should remain in the vertical-AI data-integration node as a data-engineering and AI-systems services candidate; key survival tests are customer concentration, durability of AI workloads, segment margin expansion, and proof that work is tied to deployment/evaluation rather than one-off data projects.

AVPT should be tracked as an AI-governance and data-resilience candidate; the chokepoint thesis depends on agentic AI increasing demand for data permissioning, backup, governance, compliance, and recovery across enterprise SaaS environments.

CLBT should be tracked as a regulated vertical-AI workflow candidate in digital investigations; the evidence bar should focus on ARR growth, public-sector adoption, AI-specific product usage, and privacy/regulatory constraints.

BigBear.ai was identified as a possible speculative-shadow defense AI candidate but excluded from the four-name cap; later passes should verify its 2025-2026 government contract backlog, Ask Sage exposure, dilution risk, and whether retail attention makes it less underfollowed than other defense-AI software names.

node: Vertical AI automation software, proprietary data platforms, implementation services, compliance workflows, and industrial/defense AI systems
summary: Layer 1B expands the vertical-AI software/data/workflow node using a two-lane funnel. Palantir is retained only as the high-attention reference benchmark for government/commercial AI data platforms. The discovery lane emphasizes smaller US-listed names where AI adoption may show up through data-engineering demand, AI governance/compliance, forensic/investigative workflows, or regulated public-sector automation rather than generic SaaS AI branding. No buy/sell recommendation is made; these are research candidates requiring later evidence checks.
